analysis:
Examined both primary analyses and all supplied replayed metadata, patches and source. The workflow removes paid manual dispatch, retains explicit fork opt-in for Bedrock, extends the job timeout to 60 minutes (.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml:55), and replaces the configurable fixed call cap with workload planning and a 100-call ceiling (131–136). diagnostics.py:82–84 exports completion and call-policy metrics. The added changelog and developer documentation describe bounded completion, retained findings, rerun rejection and human handoff. No independently supported regression follows from these visible changes; increased bounded resource allowances alone do not establish uncontrolled spending.
The supplied changes do not modify provider authorization, attestation, plaintext custody, hop-by-hop encryption, inference/cache isolation, billing-ledger or privileged-helper controls. TB-002/TB-011 and the indexed provider threats are not visibly invalidated. The changed CI spending and clearance contracts are distinct from those provider boundaries.
Material integration questions remain: verify the native adapter enforces an aggregate ceiling across models, depth, integration rounds and the shared repair allowance; verify timeout preserves findings and permits reporting; verify job reruns are rejected before paid calls; and verify terminal execution ('finished') cannot substitute for successful coverage/integration when granting clearance. These concerns intersect budget_scan.py, its adapter/client, the scanner entry point and threat-review-gate.py. Their necessary implementation evidence is absent from this replay (8 units omitted), so the local scanner conclusions cannot be independently validated here. Workflow settings and documentation claims at changelog.d/threat-review-automatic-completion.md:8–10, docs/developer/build.md:258–261 and docs/developer/test.md:729–735 are not proof of those controls. Further review of these changed contracts is required; missing source is a coverage limit, not an observed vulnerability.
